lessons.title: Decline extra credit plainly
lessons.when: A student asks for extra credit or an additional opportunity to raise a grade.
lessons.lesson: Decline in one sentence and point to the graded work that remains.

lessons.title: Illness without documents
lessons.when: A student reports being sick and has attached nothing.
lessons.lesson: Ask for documentation before saying anything about a makeup.

lessons.title: Office hours before email explanations
lessons.when: A student asks for help solving a homework or quiz problem.
lessons.lesson: Invite the student to office hours instead of explaining the mathematics by email.

lessons.title: Regrade route
lessons.when: A student disputes a score on graded work.
lessons.lesson: Point to the regrade form and never comment on whether the grade will change.

lessons.title: No promises on timing
lessons.when: A student asks when a quiz or exam will be handed back.
lessons.lesson: Do not promise a date; say the work will be returned as soon as grading is complete.

lessons.title: Family emergencies: brief and warm
lessons.when: A student reports a death or emergency in the family.
lessons.lesson: Open with one sentence of sympathy, give the next step, and ask no questions about the circumstances.

lessons.title: University-excused travel
lessons.when: A student athlete or band member reports upcoming university travel.
lessons.lesson: Ask for the travel letter and offer to arrange the missed quiz before the trip.

lessons.title: Missed quiz, no reason given
lessons.when: A student reports missing a quiz without explaining why.
lessons.lesson: Ask for the reason before mentioning any makeup.

lessons.title: Late online homework
lessons.when: A student asks to reopen or extend an online homework after it closed.
lessons.lesson: Online homework is not reopened; say so and point to the dropped lowest scores.

lessons.title: Grade calculation questions
lessons.when: A student asks what score they need to reach a letter grade.
lessons.lesson: Give the grade formula from the syllabus and do not compute the student's number.

lessons.title: Withdrawal advice
lessons.when: A student asks whether they should drop the course.
lessons.lesson: Never advise whether to drop; give the Q-drop date and refer the student to their advisor.

lessons.title: Accommodation letters
lessons.when: A student sends or mentions a disability accommodation letter.
lessons.lesson: Confirm receipt and ask the student to schedule exams with the testing center.

lessons.title: Technical problems during online work
lessons.when: A student reports a website or connection problem during homework or a quiz.
lessons.lesson: Ask for a screenshot and the time it happened.

lessons.title: Students afraid of failing
lessons.when: A student expresses fear of failing the course.
lessons.lesson: Acknowledge the worry in one sentence and list two concrete next steps.

lessons.title: Parent contact
lessons.when: A parent writes, or a student asks to include a parent.
lessons.lesson: Never discuss a student's record with a parent; reply only to the student.

lessons.title: Class notes requests
lessons.when: A student asks for notes or slides from a class they missed.
lessons.lesson: Point to the posted notes; do not send personal notes.

lessons.title: Exam time conflicts
lessons.when: A student reports that an exam overlaps another class or exam.
lessons.lesson: Ask for the other course's exam time in writing.

lessons.title: Thank-you messages
lessons.when: A student writes only to say thanks.
lessons.lesson: No reply is needed unless the message contains a question.

lessons.title: Recommendation letter requests
lessons.when: A student asks for a letter of recommendation.
lessons.lesson: Ask for the deadline, the program and a résumé before agreeing.

lessons.title: Seat change requests
lessons.when: A student asks to sit somewhere else during an exam.
lessons.lesson: Exam seats are assigned; change one only for a documented need.

lessons.title: Calculator questions
lessons.when: A student asks which calculator is allowed.
lessons.lesson: Quote the course calculator rule exactly.

lessons.title: Attending another section
lessons.when: A student asks to attend a different section.
lessons.lesson: A student may attend another lecture once with notice, but takes quizzes in their own section.

lessons.title: Requests for the answer key
lessons.when: A student asks for the answers or solutions to a quiz.
lessons.lesson: Do not send answer keys by email; say where the solutions are posted.

lessons.title: Students who added late
lessons.when: A student joined the course after the first week.
lessons.lesson: List the missed work and state which items are excused.

lessons.title: Oversleeping
lessons.when: A student says they overslept or forgot.
lessons.lesson: Oversleeping is not excused; say so without commentary and state what the missed work counts as.

lessons.title: Mental health disclosures
lessons.when: A student mentions anxiety or depression.
lessons.lesson: Give the counseling service contact first, then address the course question.

lessons.title: Group work complaints
lessons.when: A student complains about a teammate.
lessons.lesson: Ask the student to raise it with the group first and report back.

lessons.title: Requests to round a grade
lessons.when: A student asks to be bumped or rounded up to the next letter.
lessons.lesson: Grades are not rounded beyond the posted cutoffs; state the cutoff and decline.

lessons.title: Study advice
lessons.when: A student asks how to prepare for an exam.
lessons.lesson: Name the review sessions and the practice exam; skip general tips.

lessons.title: Unsigned messages
lessons.when: A student writes without identifying themselves or their section.
lessons.lesson: Ask for the name and section before answering.

unfaithful.rewrite: Keep all emails under about 120 words.
Never offer extra credit or makeup work to a student.
Always put an answer key and a grading rubric at the end of a quiz draft.
The instructor does not answer student email on weekends or in the evening.
Never draft exam or quiz questions for MATH 140.
This term the MATH 140 TA grades the quizzes and the exams.
This term MATH 142 has weekly drop-in review sessions; tell every student to attend them.
Give one draft and never revise it.
Write derivatives in Leibniz notation in every course.
MATH 140 quizzes are always on paper.
Solution keys show only the final answer.
